    AI Overview
    The yellow fever vaccine (e.g., YF-VAX) is a highly effective, single-dose injection providing lifelong immunity against the virus for travelers aged 9 months or older visiting high-risk areas in Africa and South America. It must be administered at least 10 days before travel at designated, certified centers. 
    Key Information: 
    • Recommendation: Recommended for travelers to endemic areas in Africa/South America and required for entry into specific countries.
    • Effectiveness & Schedule: A single dose provides 95% immunity within one week, generally lasting for life without needing a booster
      .
    • Side Effects: Generally mild, including headaches, muscle aches, and low-grade fevers. Rare but severe reactions can include allergic reactions or serious nervous system/organ issues.
    • Contraindications: Individuals over 60, pregnant/breastfeeding women, or those with compromised immune systems should consult a doctor due to higher risks.
    • Cost: Costs vary by provider and insurance, usually ranging from $150 to over $300 for the vaccine and administration fee. 
    Vaccination Certificate:
    An International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis (ICVP) is issued upon vaccination and is required for entry into many countries, validating that the vaccine was given at an authorized center. 
    Alternatives:
    If a medical exemption is needed, travellers should consult their physician.

    Recommended Age. What is the recommended age for the yellow fever vaccine?
    About this result
    Feedback
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    The recommended age for the yellow fever vaccine is 9 months or older for individuals traveling to or living in high-risk areas in Africa and South America. A single dose provides lifelong protection for most, though vaccination is generally not recommended for infants younger than 6–9 months due to increased risks. 
    Key Recommendations and Usage Examples:
    • Recommended Age: People aged 9 months through 59 years. 
    • Infants (6–8 months): Vaccination is generally avoided, but may be considered for infants 6–8 months old if traveling to high-risk areas. 
    • Infants (Under 6 months): The vaccine is contraindicated (should not be given) to infants younger than 6 months. 
    • Older Adults (60+): While not recommended for those over 59, individuals 60 or older at high risk should consult their doctor to weigh risks, as they have a higher risk of serious adverse events. 
    • International Travel: Many countries require a yellow fever vaccination certificate (ICVP) for travelers older than 9 months arriving from countries with risk of transmission. 
    • Timing: The vaccine should be administered at least 10 days before travel. 
    Synonyms/Related Terms: Yellow fever immunization, Yellow fever shot, Stamaril (vaccine brand name), and International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis (ICVP).
    Contraindications (Who should NOT get it): 
    • Infants under 6 months.
    • People with severe allergies to eggs, chicken protein, or gelatin.
    • People with weakened immune systems (HIV, thymus disorder, cancer, transplant recipients).

      Side Effects. What are the side effects of the yellow fever vaccine?
      About this result
      Feedback
      An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
      AI Overview
      Yellow fever vaccine side effects are usually mild, including low-grade fever, headache, muscle aches, and soreness at the injection site, lasting 1–3 days. While rare, severe adverse reactions such as allergic reactions, neurological issues (YEL-AND), or organ failure (YEL-AVD) can occur, particularly in individuals over 60, infants under 6 months, or those with weakened immune systems. 
      Common Side Effects
      These typically appear within 1–14 days and may include: 
      • Mild symptoms: Muscle aches, headaches, low-grade fever, and fatigue.
      • Injection site reactions: Redness, soreness, or swelling where the shot was given.
      • General discomfort: Mild diarrhea, vomiting, or nausea.
      Rare but Serious Adverse Events
      Severe reactions are very rare (approximately 1.2 cases per 100,000 vaccinations) but require immediate medical attention: 
      • Allergic Reactions (Anaphylaxis): Hives, itching, rash, or swelling of the throat/face. 
      • Yellow Fever Vaccine-Associated Neurotropic Disease (YEL-AND): Brain/nervous system issues, including high fever, confusion, or severe headaches. 
      • Yellow Fever Vaccine-Associated Viscerotropic Disease (YEL-AVD): Severe illness resembling yellow fever with organ failure (liver, kidney). 
      Precautions and Risk Groups
      The CDC recommends caution or advises against vaccination for specific groups due to higher risks of adverse effects: 
      • Age: Infants 6–8 months and adults over 60.
      • Immune System: People with HIV, cancer, or those who have had an organ transplant.
      • Pregnancy/Breastfeeding: The vaccine should generally be avoided.
      • Allergies: Those with severe allergies to eggs or other components of the vaccine.
      What to Do
      • If you experience persistent, severe, or concerning symptoms, contact a healthcare provider immediately.
      • Rest, stay hydrated, and use pain relief (e.g., paracetamol or ibuprofen) to manage mild symptoms. 
      • Do not donate blood for 14 days after vaccination.

        Brand Name. What is the brand name of the yellow fever vaccine?
        About this result
        Feedback
        An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
        AI Overview
        The primary brand name of the yellow fever vaccine used in the United States is YF-VAX, manufactured by Sanofi Pasteur. Another commonly used brand, mainly outside the United States, is Stamaril, also produced by Sanofi. Both are live, attenuated vaccines designed to prevent yellow fever. 
        • YF-VAX: Licensed in the US, widely available for travelers. 
        • Stamaril: Used in many countries globally but not licensed in the US. 
        Both vaccines offer long-term or lifelong protection, often requiring only one dose for international certification.

          Active Ingredients. What are the active ingredients in the yellow fever vaccine?
          About this result
          Feedback
          An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
          AI Overview
          The active ingredient in the yellow fever vaccine is a live, attenuated (weakened) strain of the yellow fever virus, specifically the 17D strain. It is cultured in chicken embryos. The vaccine contains no preservatives, but stabilizer ingredients like sorbitol and gelatin are typically included. 
          Key Details About Active Ingredients:
          • Live Virus: The vaccine contains a weakened form of the virus that triggers an immune response without causing the disease. 
          • Strains: The 17D-204 strain is used in many vaccines (e.g., YF-VAX). 
          • Potency: The vaccine is formulated to contain a specific concentration, not less than
            4.74 log104.74 log sub 10
            plaque-forming units (PFU) per 0.5 mL dose.             
          • Components: The vaccine contains egg protein (from the manufacturing process). 
          • Stabilizers: Sorbitol and gelatin are added to maintain the stability of the live virus. 
          Inactive Ingredients (Reconstituent): 
          • Sodium Chloride Injection (USP): This is used to dissolve the freeze-dried (lyophilized) vaccine powder before administration.

            How many times do you need to get the yellow fever vaccine?
            The World Health Organization Strategic Advisory Group of Experts in Immunization concluded in April 2013 that a single primary dose of yellow fever vaccine is sufficient to confer sustained immunity and lifelong protection against yellow fever disease, and a booster dose of the vaccine is not needed.
